title: The Emerging-Market AI Divide: How World Bank Plans To Democratise 'Small AI' For Small Businesses
source_used: The Nation Thailand (12 Oct 2026), News 1st (16 Oct 2026), VTV via Vietnam.vn; NDTV Profit was blocked
key_facts: World Bank Group President Ajay Banga urged emerging economies to focus on practical AI applications rather than compete with the US and China on the largest AI models (Nation Thailand, 12 Oct 2026).
He calls this 'small AI': accessible, affordable, purpose-built applications for local needs in healthcare, agriculture, education and financial services.
He cited a World Bank farmer tool launched in India and clinic diagnosis in Indonesia as examples.
He said reliable electricity and internet connectivity must come before countries can fully benefit from AI.

News 1st (16 Oct 2026): 1.2 billion young people are expected to enter the labour market while only around 400 million jobs are projected; the World Bank is working on electricity, connectivity, devices and safeguards, and on a strategy to help small and medium-sized firms get finance and markets.

VTV: Thailand showed an AI tool called 'Nok Krasip' to help small businesses reach capital and manage stock; Thai finance minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas wants startups, small firms and universities to take part in AI tools.
The Nation says the World Bank Group mobilised a record US$112 billion in private capital in fiscal year 2026.
quote_evidence: Banga urged emerging economies to focus on practical applications of artificial intelligence rather than trying to compete directly with the United States and China in developing the largest AI models.
Banga stressed that reliable electricity and internet connectivity must come before countries can fully benefit from AI.

World Bank Group President Ajay Banga has warned that the global economy faces a major employment challenge over the next decade, with 1.2 billion young people expected to enter the labour market while only around 400 million jobs are projected to be created.
why_it_matters_hint: The World Bank is steering developing countries toward cheap, local AI tools for small businesses and jobs.
notes: Desk-built from three outlets because NDTV Profit was blocked; the 1.2 billion horizon differs between outlets.
